Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) with mshr for geometry and mesh generation.
The domain is a rectangular strip Ω = (0, 1.0) × (0, 0.20) m containing two circular holes of radius 0.04 m centred at (0.40, 0.10) m and (0.60, 0.10) m.
Generate the mesh with a target cell size of approximately 0.01–0.02 m, aiming for roughly 2000–5000 quadrilateral cells total, ensuring adequate resolution on both hole boundaries.
The model is a large-deformation isotropic quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean solid in plane strain, solved with a mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation.
The unknowns are the displacement field u = (u_x, u_y) and the hydrostatic pressure p.
The material parameters are Young's modulus E = 5 MPa and Poisson's ratio ν = 0.49, giving shear modulus μ = E / (2(1 + ν)).
The strain energy density is W = (μ/2)(I₁ − 3) + (λ/2)(J − 1)² where I₁ = tr(F·Fᵀ) and J = det(F), with the plane-strain deformation gradient F having F₃₃ = 1.
The mixed weak form consists of two equations: (1) the momentum balance ∫_Ω [μ(F − F⁻ᵀ) + p·F⁻ᵀ] : δF dΩ = external work for all test functions δu, and (2) the incompressibility constraint ∫_Ω δp·(J − 1) dΩ = 0 for all test functions δp.
In the momentum equation, the external work includes the prescribed right-edge displacement (handled via Dirlet BC) and the hole pressure tractions.
On the left edge (x = 0), impose the Dirichlet condition u = (0, 0).
On the right edge (x = 1.0), impose the Dirichlet condition u = (0.060, 0).
On each circular hole boundary, apply a uniform pressure traction P_hole = 0.10 MPa directed along the outward reference (undeformed) normal n_ref, contributing ∫_{hole} P_hole · n_ref · δu dS to the external work in the weak form.
The top edge (y = 0.20) and bottom edge (y = 0) are traction-free (no Neumann contribution).
Solve the nonlinear system using Newton–Raphson iteration with a residual convergence tolerance of 1e−8 and a maximum of 30 iterations.
Use a stable mixed finite element pair for (u, p), such as P2 for displacement and P1 for pressure, or P1 for displacement and P0 (discontinuous) for pressure.
After convergence, compute the Cauchy stress σ = (μ/J)(F·Fᵀ) + λ(J−1)·I in the plane-strain sense, including the σ_zz component.
Compute the von Mises stress as σ_vm = sqrt((1/2)[(σ_xx − σ_yy)² + (σ_yy − σ_zz)² + (σ_zz − σ_xx)² + 6σ_xy²]).
Save a colour map of the pressure field p as the file q14_p.png.
Save a colour map of the von Mises stress field as the file q14_vm.png.
Save the displacement field in XDMF format.
